title: Export model release notes with Private upgrade bundles (offline + rollback friendly)
creator: Michael Nguyen
project: Model Metadata Schema v1 + Changelog Generator
description:
Private customers (VPC/on-prem, sometimes air-gapped) receive upgrades as signed upgrade bundles. They need a deterministic, exportable set of release notes for *exactly* what changed in the bundle (models + serving/runtime components where applicable) with clear deprecation/rollback guidance.

Today, customer-visible release notes are primarily Console/docs surfaces and may not be available/accessible in offline environments. This ticket adds an export step that packages generated release notes alongside Private upgrade artifacts, with strict redaction guarantees (public-only fields), stable IDs for auditability, and offline-friendly formats.

Drivers:
- SUP-28455: customer asks for upgrade bundle release notes + deprecation timeline
- Enterprise security reviews (e.g., Northbridge) explicitly call out change visibility + audit trails as procurement blockers

Non-goals (for this ticket):
- Building a new notification system (email/webhooks)
- Rewriting historical Private release notes beyond minimal backfill
- Changing the changelog taxonomy/style guide (consume what exists)

Primary stakeholders: Connor O'Brien (Release Eng), Kira Thompson (Private docs), Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin (Security), Dev Patel (Support/CS).
problem_statement: Private upgrades are frequently performed in restricted environments where Redwood Console and public docs are unavailable. Without a bundle-embedded, verifiable release note export, customers cannot meet internal change-management requirements, and Support cannot quickly align reported regressions to exact bundle contents. Additionally, release notes must not leak internal-only fields and must be stable across rebuilds (deterministic output) for audits.
proposed_solution:
Add a bundle export artifact produced during the Private upgrade bundle build:
1) Resolve the set of included model versions/variants/quantization profiles (and any pinned runtime/compiler component versions if included in bundle manifest).
2) Query/generate release notes from the changelog generator for the resolved set (public view).
3) Write a deterministic export directory inside the bundle (e.g., /release-notes/) containing:
   - release-notes.jsonl (one entry per change event / release note item)
   - release-notes.md (human-readable rollup summary)
   - index.json (manifest + checksums + schema versions)
   - optional: release-notes.rss (only if requested by Docs; not required for Private)
4) Include checksums in the bundle manifest and ensure bundle signing covers the release note directory.

All content is generated from the same canonical event stream used for Console/docs, but with a strict 'publicOnly=true' rendering mode enforced at generation time and validated in CI.
artifact_spec:
Location in bundle:
- /release-notes/index.json
- /release-notes/release-notes.jsonl
- /release-notes/release-notes.md

Format requirements:
- index.json: includes generator version, schema versions, generation timestamp (UTC), bundle_id, and sha256 for each file.
- release-notes.jsonl: each line is a single release note item with a stable id (event_id), model_id, model_version, category (security/breaking/perf/quality/bugfix/deprecation), severity (info/medium/high), affected_deployments (must include Private), and links (docs URL only if public).
- release-notes.md: top-level summary + per-model sections + explicit 'How to roll back' references.

Determinism:
- Sort order must be stable: (published_at asc, model_id asc, event_id asc)
- Normalize whitespace; no environment-specific paths; no embedding of internal hostnames
- Timestamps: allow build timestamp only in index.json; content entries should use event timestamps
offline_constraints:
Assume:
- No outbound network access at install time
- Limited tooling on customer side (must be readable as plain text/JSON)
- Customers often attach bundle artifacts to internal tickets; files must be self-contained

Therefore:
- Must not require Console access to interpret
- Must not include references that require authentication (ok to include public docs URLs, but must remain optional)
- Must not include dynamic content generation at install time (export is build-time only)
acceptance_criteria: Private upgrade bundle contains /release-notes/ directory with index.json, release-notes.jsonl, and release-notes.md
Export includes only customer-visible (public) fields; any internal_only fields are excluded even if present in upstream events
Export is deterministic across rebuilds given the same input event set (byte-for-byte equality for jsonl/md; index.json may differ only by generated_at)
Bundle signing includes the release note files (tamper-evident)
Support can map a customer-reported regression to bundle_id + event_id(s) using exported artifacts
CI check fails if release note export would include redacted fields or missing required public fields for any included model version
implementation_notes:
Planned implementation (subject to review with Release Eng):
- Add a step to the Private bundle build pipeline (private-bundler) called export_release_notes.
- Inputs:
  - bundle_id
  - bundle manifest listing included model versions + profiles
  - changelog generator endpoint/library (prefer library call inside bundler build container to avoid network dependency)
  - rendering flags: deployment=private, audience=public
- Output directory staged into bundle before signing.

Open question: service vs library
- If generator is only reachable as a service, we risk build breaks when building offline/isolated bundles. Prefer to vendor the generator library into bundler, with pinned templates + taxonomy version.
- If we must call a service, do so at build time in Redwood infra; never at customer install time. Also must cache response and include it in bundle.

Edge cases:
- Bundle includes models whose release notes are embargoed (customer-specific or not yet public). Proposed behavior: include a placeholder entry 'Details available upon request' with event_id, category, severity, and a support contact reference; keep actual content internal. (Needs PM + Security sign-off.)
- Bundle includes a model version without changelog entries (e.g., backfill gap). Proposed behavior: include a minimal autogenerated 'Version included in this bundle; details not available' entry; emit internal warning metric and fail CI only if model is marked 'requires_release_notes=true'.
qa_plan:
Test matrix (Leila + QA automation):
- E2E: build a bundle with 2 model updates + 1 deprecation notice, verify exported files present and sorted deterministically.
- Redaction: inject internal_only fields into a fixture event, ensure they do not appear in jsonl/md.
- Determinism: run the same build twice, diff artifacts; expect identical jsonl/md.
- Tamper: modify a release note file after signing; verify signature/manifest verification fails.
- Missing notes: include a model version with no changelog entries; verify placeholder behavior and CI policy enforcement.

Add unit tests around:
- stable ordering
- markdown renderer escaping
- checksum generation
rollout_plan:
1) Dogfood: generate exports for internal staging Private bundles for 1 week.
2) Beta: enable for 1-2 enterprise Private accounts (coordinate via Liam O'Rourke + CS). Provide a short guide for where to find /release-notes/ and how to interpret.
3) GA: enable by default for all Private upgrade bundles; update docs/runbook templates used by Support.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risks:
- Accidental leakage of internal-only details into Private bundle artifacts.
  - Mitigation: enforce audience=public at renderer boundary; add golden tests; add CI scanner for banned fields/strings.
- Non-deterministic exports due to template changes or environment differences.
  - Mitigation: version templates; pin taxonomy version; stable sorting; normalize newlines; separate index.json timestamp.
- Customers interpret 'quality' claims as guarantees.
  - Mitigation: ensure generated content follows the style guide language; avoid metrics unless flagged safe; include 'may vary by workload' footer.
- Bundler/generator coupling increases release friction.
  - Mitigation: keep export step optional behind a feature flag initially; treat generator library as a small dependency with clear semver.
comments: 2025-10-14 (Connor O'Brien): Please ensure the export is produced *before* bundle signing and included in the signed manifest. Also: build should not require access to docs.redwood.ai; any URLs must be static strings.

2025-10-16 (Marcus Lin): Treat release note export as customer-visible artifact. Redaction policy must be identical to public docs. Add a test that verifies internal-only keys never appear (e.g., internal_summary, incident_links, account_names).

2025-10-18 (Kira Thompson): Markdown rollup is important for change advisory boards. Please include a 'Upgrade impact' header per model and a 'Rollback' subsection that points to the relevant section of the Private upgrade guide.
2025-10-22 (Dev Patel): Support asks for stable identifiers. If we can include event_id and model_version in jsonl, we can reference those in escalations without screenshots from Console.

2025-10-27 (Diego Santos): Implementing as a library call in private-bundler to avoid service dependency. I’ll sync with Quentin/Jada on how to resolve model_version -> changelog entries when multiple profiles exist in a single bundle.

definition_of_done:
Done when:
- Export step is enabled in staging, producing signed /release-notes/ artifacts.
- QA matrix passes, including determinism and redaction.
- Docs/runbook reference for Private customers is updated (Kira) and Support has a short internal playbook for locating artifacts.
- Security review sign-off recorded in ticket comments and feature flag is set to on for GA.
